images.observation: Clean framed entrance segment; existing white portico, glazing and warm tile-like wall preserved. Right artificial wall side neutral. Changed left step end is mostly hidden from this right-front view.

Broad artificial back, side and top closures remain neutral. The exposed staircase end beyond the wall is stone grey and its stepped outline remains intact; no window or facade was painted onto the crop.

Front elevation remains clean, with open portico, unequal original lower window/door groups and two upper groups. Original colors remain unchanged; the left step-end correction is edge-on from this view.

Low orthographic source-direction view keeps the real portico opening and dark lightweight canopy beams intact. Existing window/door groups stay colored. The authored base underside is visible in this low-angle display view; it is not a photographed ground surface.

The genuine stair left-end stepped profile is continuous stone grey, matching the original right-end treatment. The taller artificial wall-side closure stays neutral, with a clear spatial gap from the step end.
Original stone stair right end and portico remain unchanged; right artificial wall side stays neutral. No additional openings or colored panels appear on the wall cut.
Projected beam and canopies retain original colors. Broad upper artificial wall closure remains neutral; no full roof has been invented. Entire partial footprint and base remain intact.

Original assignment comparison is visually almost identical from this right-front angle because the altered left step end is largely occluded. Window groups, canopy, columns and wall colors match the repaired front.

The original stair left end appears neutral darker grey. Comparison with repaired rear shows that small stepped end alone becomes continuous stone grey; the broad artificial back, side and top remain neutral and identical.
